summary: GA4 web-property cutover, explicit source-history retention, future tracker and goal rebuild, and verified reversible DataFast adoption.

capabilities.notes: DataFast's current FAQ says historical import is Plausible-only for now and Google Analytics is next. No documented GA4 CSV, Data API, or BigQuery ingestion path warrants importing historical traffic, events, revenue, attribution, audiences, or user data.

Required source-only control: archive approved GA4 aggregate reports, retention settings, and existing BigQuery evidence outside DataFast for source retention and fixed-date baselines. This does not create target history; a new GA4 BigQuery link does not provide retrospective backfill.

Record the GA4 reporting timezone and DataFast website timezone. They must match before production collection, or an owner must approve a documented conversion and fixed date-boundary convention for every comparison.

Install the documented tracker only after an additive dry run. Client markup uses the approved DataFast trackingId (dfid_...), while dashboard/API read-back uses websiteId; preserve GA4 during parallel verification and make reruns idempotent by trackingId plus location.

DataFast documents Google Tag Manager and CMS integrations, but publication is human-owned. After the dry-run inventory, add one approved target tag; do not overwrite, disable, or remove the GA4 tag before acceptance.

Inspect GA4 event/key-event configuration and source instrumentation, then rebuild accepted future DataFast goals from a mapping ledger. Event names, custom definitions, and semantics are not a one-to-one migration.

Review server-side events, identity, and measurement behavior independently. Never copy GA Measurement Protocol secrets or historic identifiers; use documented target interfaces only after privacy and semantic approval.

Rebuild only approved DataFast funnels, reports, and shares after reviewing their filters, stages, attribution, and intended audience. No documented cross-provider dashboard importer warrants an automatic copy.

Reconnect Google Search Console in the DataFast target only after the owner approves the Google authorization and matching verified property. Treat it as a fresh integration, not a copied source link.

GA4 audiences, Google Ads links, remarketing lists, and advertising activation have no documented automatic DataFast target migration. Preserve and redesign them under a separately approved advertising plan.
Connect an approved DataFast payment provider as a fresh owner-approved dashboard integration. Historical GA4 ecommerce, revenue, attribution, and financial records are not imported.

Implement a DataFast Payment API or checkout-metadata integration only after financial, privacy, and semantic approval. Use a genuine target df_ key only where required, preserve idempotency, and never replay historic GA4 revenue or duplicate payment events.

Cookie/cookieless mode, consent, cross-domain topology, referral/internal-traffic exclusions, proxy, and CSP are legal/product decisions. DataFast collection and attribution behavior can differ from GA4.
Create target access, roles, subscriptions, and settings only with owner approval. Do not copy provider permissions, property settings, or billing state automatically.

Google Analytics Data API OAuth/service-account access and a target-restricted DataFast dft_ token can automate aggregate baselines and read-back. Use analytics:read for metrics; add settings:read, goals:read, or funnels:read only for those checks, and websites:read only to list/select the target. They are optional; reserve df_ website keys for genuine server-side operations.
